note: Skeptic Shark, operator angle. Judged only against the five numbered North Star surfaces. Heartbeat at `heartbeat.json`.

findings.criterion: 3 — a .py or .R row that is short (≤ 120 lines) or marked as a notebook (`# %%` cells, or `# notebook` in its first lines) is converted once … and opened in JupyterLab; longer code opens in the editor … and the row says which
findings.message: P1.1 HOLDs the entire `open_kind` module until John re-ratifies that a long `# %%` / `# notebook` file opens as a notebook. Criterion 3 already locks that marker rule, and the quote independently locks the short/long split. Packaging the override beside the classifier parks both. With no classifier, no row can say "notebook" / "editor", and a 20-line `.py` has no decision that sends it to a notebook. The operator's first visible distinction is gated on a question the North Star already answered.

findings.criterion: 1 — a project's own JupyterLab, managed like a preview: started on demand (cwd = the project folder) on an OS-assigned free port that is never 8777, with its own token, registered, listed, stoppable, reaped when dead
findings.message: P2.1 spends zero until John picks (A) the existing jupyter-serve or (B) a new per-project lab. Criterion 1 is (B). The HOLD then parks start/probe/ensure, `fake_lab`, the labs endpoints, the boot reap, and the `/notebook` 302 Location. There is no operator-visible fallback: no project lab, no stop control, no restart of a dead lab. Re-asking the North Star as a one-liner leaves criterion 1 unimplemented while later phases still talk as if a lab exists.

findings.topic: clickable rows wired to a HOLD open
findings.criterion: 2 — a .ipynb row (register, plan outline, files tile) opens in a new window at the lab's /lab/tree/<rel> for that file, starting or restarting the lab if needed — never a blank page
findings.message: Phase 3 KEEPs `open_kind` on register rows, the delivRow `/notebook` rewrite, and files-tile `window.open` of that route. Phase 2's lab dispatch, `ensure_lab`, and never-blank interstitial are HOLD. John will see a chip and a clickable row. One implementation reads the KEEP list and ships hrefs at a missing or half-built route (blank/404/hung tab). The other skips the rewrite because `open_kind` never shipped, so the same rows stay read-only artifacts. Either way a notebook row does not open in JupyterLab. The plan has no operator contract for what a click does while those HOLDs stand.

findings.topic: never-blank gated on first blank click
findings.criterion: 2 — a stale or dead lab is restarted, never a blank page
findings.message: The interstitial is HOLD until "a recorded click that is blank or hung under a blocking 302-after-probe." Criterion 2 already forbids that click. Remaining path is a GET `/notebook` that waits up to 20s for a probe, then 302s or errors — a spinnerless tab on the dashboard origin, which is a blank page. The rebuild trigger makes John the first failing test instead of treating never-blank as a ship rule. A lab that is "up on first probe" skips the page; the cold start, the missing-jupyter case, and the hung pid are exactly when he clicks.

findings.topic: live-link sign-off is markup not an open
findings.criterion: 5 — a live-link row opens (Playwright screenshots); 4 — a Where cell that is a localhost / 127.0.0.1 / tailnet-name URL renders as a link (new window) (journal 0110 — a JupyterLab or Shiny address reachable from the register and the plan without a launch page)
findings.message: Sign-off (d) only asserts the row is an `<a>` whose href has no `token=` and whose rel contains noopener, then screenshots that. It does not navigate. Criterion 5 says the live-link row opens. Criterion 4's 0110 clause is reachable, not merely painted. A screenshot of a link is the launch-page workaround in thinner clothing: John still cannot tell whether the address works. The fixture `http://gwl-server:<lab port or 8888>/lab` cannot even be written honestly — the lab port is OS-assigned at start, and 8888 is not that lab.

findings.topic: tailnet live-link cannot reach loopback lab
findings.section: Phase 1 bind + Phase 3 stale-by-design + Phase 4 fixture
findings.criterion: 4 — a Where cell that is a http://<this machine's tailnet name>/… URL renders as a link (new window); journal 0110 — a JupyterLab address reachable from the register without a launch page
findings.message: The managed lab binds `--ip=127.0.0.1` with `allow_remote_access=False`; tailnet bind is explicitly deferred. Phase 3 then KEEPs `where_for(url=)` so a campaign can register a JupyterLab address, and parks current-port rendering with "a registered lab URL may go stale, by design." Phase 5 still uses a `gwl-server` live-link as the proof row. That hostname will not connect to a loopback-only lab, and an OS-assigned port baked into DELIVERABLES.md is dead on the next start. This is the 0110 dead JupyterLab address, now as a specified outcome. Path-rows via `/notebook` do not save a Where cell that is the URL criterion 4 exists to make clickable.

findings.topic: editor sign-off proves vscode:// not code -r
findings.criterion: 3 — longer code opens in the editor (VS Code on this machine, `code -r <file>`); 5 — a long .py opens in the editor (Playwright screenshots)
findings.message: Criterion 3 names `code -r`. The editor element still dual-fires `location.assign(vscode://file/<abs>)` and the editor seam; vscode:// is HOLD until a recorded click where `code -r` failed. Sign-off (c) then captures a `vscode://file/` navigation request and screenshots that browser page, and defers proving VS Code raised the file as a human glance. The operator proof is the HOLD URI on a tab that says "Opening … in the editor," not the editor window. Dual-fire, if the URI leaks through, can also open the file twice. The North Star editor path is unshown.

findings.criterion: 2 — starting or restarting the lab if needed — never a blank page; a stale or dead lab is restarted
findings.message: `ensure_lab` treats a live pid whose `/api/status` probe fails twice as dead, tree-kills it, and starts fresh, with a 20s health timeout. Criterion 2 restarts stale or dead labs, not slow ones. A cold JupyterLab on this machine that is still binding when the probe expires is killed mid-boot. The next click starts another. The file is never selected; with P3.3 HOLD there is no progress page, only a hung `/notebook` tab. Restart-on-hung becomes restart-on-not-ready-yet, which is how "come up every time" becomes "never stays up."

findings.topic: R kernel deferred while rows claim ir
findings.section: Phase 1 deferred / Phase 0 writer / Phase 4 sign-off
findings.criterion: 3 — kernel python3 or ir; Statement — short code as a Jupyter notebook in the project's own JupyterLab (Python and R kernels)
findings.message: `to_notebook` stamps `.R` with kernelspec `ir`. R kernel install is deferred. Sign-off skips the `.R` row if IRkernel is absent, "honestly." The operator who clicks a short `.R` still gets a sibling notebook that names a kernel the lab does not have. Execution-on-open is a non-goal; shipping an R kernel in the lab is not — the statement is Python and R kernels, not Python plus an `ir` label. A skipped sign-off row is not an R open. The row's "notebook" chip will lie about where that file runs.

findings.criterion: 3 — converted once to a sibling one-cell .ipynb
findings.message: Criterion 3 is one-cell. P1.3 HOLD says omit `marker_split` from `to_notebook`, the route, and the tests. The near-term text still specifies `marker_split=True`, a Judge flag, shared-writer both-paths, tests for both, and P3.2 still passes the flag into the route. An implementer following the phase body builds per-cell conversion for `# %%` files; one following the HOLD table does not. John clicking a marked file cannot know whether he gets one cell or many. A HOLD that leaves the spend in the spec is not a cut. One-cell is already locked — the leftover flag is unearned operator-visible behaviour.
